text: Enforce idea permissions on the GitHub remote: required check on pull requests
description:
Felix 2026-11-11: constraints such as who is allowed to edit an idea could be enforced on the GitHub side, on the remote repository. People can still run Aimparency for themselves; if they want the permission system enforced, they do it this way. The UI allows an action only if the permissions are fine, and a GitHub App enforces that permissions were not exceeded.

Checked against GitHub's documentation (2026-11-11):
- github.com cannot run custom code at push time; pre-receive hooks exist only on GitHub Enterprise Server. A push cannot be rejected by a rule like "this person may not edit this idea".
- Push rules (restrict file paths) are not per person, hold at most 200 entries and apply only to private and internal repositories.
- What works: a ruleset on main that requires a pull request and a status check, with a specific GitHub App selected as the only accepted source of that check. The app compares the idea files a pull request changes with the author's rights and reports pass or fail.
- Bypass list of a ruleset: roles, teams, GitHub Apps; so a hosted Aimparency acting as the app, and repository admins, can keep pushing directly.
- CODEOWNERS with "require review from code owners" is a built-in form of "the owner must approve", per file, for people or teams with write access; file under 3 MB. It knows no manager or write levels.

Requirement that follows: the check must read owners and levels from the target branch, not from the pull request, or people could grant themselves rights in the same change.

status.comment: Explored on 2026-11-11, not decided. Feasible on github.com as a required pull-request check from a GitHub App; not feasible as a rejection of direct pushes. Depends on fcb38df6 (owners and levels stored in the idea files). Not checked: which GitHub plans allow rulesets on private repositories.
